summary.short: Adds Subchapter T to New York City's rules requiring employers and employment agencies using automated employment decision tools (AEDTs) in hiring or promotion to obtain a bias audit within one year before use, publish audit results and distribution date, and give candidates and employees notice and data-related information.
summary.long: Adds Subchapter T (§§ 5-300 to 5-304) to Chapter 5 of Title 6 of the Rules of the City of New York, governing automated employment decision tools (AEDTs). Section 5-300 defines AEDT by reference to § 20-870 of the Administrative Code and defines bias audit, independent auditor, impact ratio, selection rate, scoring rate, historical data and test data. Section 5-301 bars an employer or employment agency from using or continuing to use an AEDT if more than one year has passed since its most recent bias audit, and sets minimum audit calculations by sex, race/ethnicity and intersectional categories, with an optional exclusion for categories under 2% of the data. Section 5-302 sets data requirements, allowing historical data from one or more employers and test data where historical data is insufficient. Section 5-303 requires publication before use of the audit date, a summary of results and the distribution date on the employment website, kept for at least six months after last use. Section 5-304 sets notice methods for city candidates and employees at least 10 business days before use, and requires data retention, data type and data source disclosures with written requests answered within 30 days. The text states no effective date and contains no penalty provisions.

notes: Section 1 of a rule amendment adding Subchapter T (§§ 5-300 to 5-304). The text states no adoption date, effective date or enabling authority, so no legal_basis relation is recorded. Several definitions incorporate outside texts by reference (Administrative Code §§ 20-870 and 20-871, 6 RCNY § 5-249, 42 U.S.C. § 2000e-8(c), 29 C.F.R. § 1602.7, EEO-1); their content is not in the document. The examples in §§ 5-301 and 5-302 are shown with their data omitted. Employers and employment agencies, the addressees, are generic roles and are not listed as entities.

definitions.defined_in: Administrative Code of the City of New York § 20-870

evidence.quote: “Bias audit” means “Bias audit” as defined by § 20-870 of the Code.

definitions.defined_in: Administrative Code of the City of New York § 20-870

evidence.quote: “Employment decision” means “Employment decision” as defined by § 20-870 of the Code.
“Employment agency” means “Employment agency” as defined by 6 RCNY § 5-249.

“Candidate for employment” means a person who has applied for a specific employment position by submitting the necessary information or items in the format required by the employer or employment agency.
“Screen” means to make a determination about whether a candidate for employment or employee being considered for promotion should be selected or advanced in the hiring or promotion process.
“Independent auditor” means a person or group that is capable of exercising objective and impartial judgment on all issues within the scope of a bias audit of an AEDT.
“Distribution date” means the date the employer or employment agency began using a specific AEDT.
“Historical data” means data collected during an employer or employment agency’s use of an AEDT to assess candidates for employment or employees for promotion.
“Test data” means data used to conduct a bias audit that is not historical data.

definitions.defined_in: title 42 of the United States Code, section 2000e-8(c); part 1602.7 of title 29 of the Code of Federal Regulations (as cited in the text)

evidence.quote: “Category” means any component 1 category required to be reported by employers pursuant to subsection (c) of section 2000e-8 of title 42 of the United States Code

“Impact ratio” means either (1) the selection rate for a category divided by the selection rate of the most selected category or (2) the scoring rate for a category divided by the scoring rate for the highest scoring category.

obligations.summary: An employer or employment agency may not use or continue to use an AEDT if more than one year has passed since the most recent bias audit. Employment agencies are named in the text but have no matching role in the addressee list.
obligations.conditional_on: more than one year has passed since the most recent bias audit of the AEDT

evidence.quote: An employer or employment agency may not use or continue to use an AEDT if more than one year has passed since the most recent bias audit of the AEDT.

obligations.summary: A bias audit must, at a minimum, calculate selection rates and impact ratios for each category and separately for sex, race/ethnicity and intersectional categories. Where an AEDT scores candidates, it must instead calculate the median score, scoring rates and impact ratios, and indicate the number of individuals in unknown categories.

obligations.summary: An independent auditor may exclude from the impact ratio calculations a category that represents less than 2% of the data, but must then include its justification and the number of applicants and the scoring or selection rate for the excluded category in the summary of results.

evidence.quote: an independent auditor may exclude a category that represents less than 2% of the data being used for the bias audit from the required calculations for impact ratio.

obligations.summary: An auditor is not an independent auditor of an AEDT if it was involved in using, developing or distributing the tool, has an employment relationship with the employer or vendor, or has a direct or material indirect financial interest in them.

evidence.quote: A bias audit conducted pursuant to section 5-301 of this Chapter must use historical data of the AEDT.

obligations.summary: An employer or employment agency may rely on a bias audit that uses other employers' historical data only if it provided its own historical data from its use of the AEDT to the independent auditor, or if it has never used the AEDT.

A hyperlink to the results may satisfy this.

enforcement.note: The fetched rule text (Subchapter T, §§ 5-300 to 5-304) states no penalties, fines, or other sanctions. It refers to § 20-871 of the Administrative Code for notice duties, but that section is not reproduced in this document, so any sanction regime it contains is not annotated here.
